children: HDFC Bank shares remained largely steady after gaining nearly 3 per cent in the previous session as the lender advanced its CEO succession process with two names submitted to the RBI
HDFC Bank shares traded largely flat on Wednesday after rising nearly 3 per cent in the previous session, as investors assessed the latest developments in the private lender’s CEO succession process.
The stock was trading around Rs 716 during late morning trade, after opening at Rs 714.90 and touching an intraday high of Rs 720.30. It had closed at Rs 716.55 in the previous session.

The recent movement follows HDFC Bank’s decision to submit two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for the position of managing director and chief executive officer. The names were submitted in order of preference along with the proposed remuneration for a three-year term. The bank has not disclosed the identities of the candidates.
The development marks a formal step in the succession process for Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose second term as HDFC Bank’s MD and CEO ends in October 2026.

The bank’s board has also made changes to strengthen its leadership structure. V Srinivasa Rangan was reappointed as a whole-time director, while Chief Credit Officer Jimmy Tata was appointed to the board in the same capacity. HDFC Bank has also proposed creating a fourth whole-time director position for the incoming CEO.

Reports have identified Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha as an internal contender, although the bank has not officially disclosed the candidates. An external banking executive is also understood to be in consideration.
The succession process has become a key factor for investors as HDFC Bank works through a period of balance-sheet expansion following its merger with HDFC Ltd.

The stock has remained under pressure this year, making the leadership transition an important near-term focus for the market. The previous session’s rise followed the submission of the candidates to the RBI, suggesting that greater clarity around the succession process was being closely watched by investors.
The RBI’s decision on the proposed candidates will now be closely monitored, followed by the required shareholder approval process.
